title: Outsider Reactions: The Bid-Ask Spread
section_job: Profile the measure's outsider-reaction behavior on the post-call information environment. Two findings: (a) the Q&A RESIDUAL is inert to the bid-ask spread across all twelve specifications -- extending DWZ's residual market-null (shown for price and volume) to a liquidity outcome DWZ did not test; (b) the scripted PRESENTATION uncertainty widens the contemporaneous spread -- consistent with BGT 2018's positive presentation-language / information-asymmetry (obfuscation) relation and with DWZ's finding that the presentation, not the residual, is what outsiders respond to. Together they establish a channel asymmetry and SHIELD the Section 3 run-up from an outsider-reaction reading.
spine: P1 setup + double anchor (spread = info-asymmetry proxy over BGT's 25-day window; DWZ residual market-null prior + never tested liquidity; BGT presentation/response opposite signs) -> P2 RESIDUAL null all 12 (extends DWZ to liquidity) -> P3 PRESENTATION positive on contemporaneous spread, hedged (one-tailed; 4/6; firm-FE specs hold; lead null) consistent with BGT obfuscation + DWZ presentation-moves-outsiders -> P4 synthesis: channel asymmetry + Section 3 identification shield.
thin_claim: Residual is null on the post-call spread in every specification (consistent with DWZ's residual market-inertness, extended to liquidity; a failure to find, not a powered equivalence test). Presentation uncertainty is positively associated with the contemporaneous spread (one-tailed; four of six contemporaneous specs; all three firm-FE specs; null one quarter ahead), consistent with BGT's obfuscation component. The split shields the Section 3 run-up: outsiders do not price the residual, so the run-up is a private insider signal.
register_global: spread coefficients are in the table's basis-point-scaled units (Spread_25D x 10^4); report as shown, do not convert
speech-component IVs are tested ONE-TAILED (beta>0) per the table note; state one-tailed as an honest secondary qualifier
our linguistic measure is uncertainty-WORD frequency (DWZ), NOT BGT's Fog complexity; BGT alignment is in DIRECTION, not identical construct
regressions include a lagged dependent variable (persistence-adjusted association)

the channel split is described as two per-component facts (the presentation positively associated with the spread; the residual not detectably associated), consistent with a channel difference, never as a tested between-component difference. State once that the difference between the two components is not tested directly. This register also governs the abstract, the introduction, and the conclusion (advisor, 2026-06-15).

intent.statement: Pose the question and set the two priors. We ask whether the speech-uncertainty signal moves the post-call information environment, proxied by the bid-ask spread over the 25-trading-day window beginning on the call date (BGT 2018; the spread is the standard adverse-selection / information-asymmetry proxy). DWZ found that neither the presentation nor the residual uncertainty is associated with stock price or volume responses, and that the residual explains little of the market reaction, but DWZ never tested liquidity. BGT show that call language relates to information asymmetry with OPPOSITE signs for the scripted presentation (positive, obfuscation) and the spontaneous response (negative, informative). We decompose the spread by the three DWZ speech components.
intent.reason: The section's nulls and the presentation positive are only informative against a stated prior and a validated outcome proxy. P1 must (a) license the spread as an information-asymmetry proxy on BGT's own window, and (b) plant BOTH priors so P2 reads as an extension of DWZ and P3 reads as a confirmation of BGT -- the double anchor is the spine.

paragraphs.final_prose: A natural further question is whether the speech-uncertainty signal travels beyond the firm to the outside information environment. We measure that environment by the bid-ask spread, a standard adverse-selection proxy, taken over the twenty-five trading days that begin on the call date, the post-call window of \citet{bgt2018}, who study the same two-segment structure. Two priors frame the test. \citet{dwz} report that neither the presentation nor the residual component of uncertainty is associated with stock price or volume responses, and that the residual explains little of the market reaction, but they do not examine any liquidity outcome. \citet{bgt2018} show that the language of a call relates to information asymmetry with opposite signs across the call's two segments: complexity in the scripted presentation is positively associated with information asymmetry, while complexity in the spontaneous response is negatively associated with it. We therefore regress the post-call spread on the three speech components of Section~2.3, retaining the lagged spread and the usual controls, and read the components one at a time.

intent.statement: The residual is inert. UncResCEO carries no association with the post-call spread in any of the twelve specifications: contemporaneously the coefficients are small and insignificant (between -0.0594 and -0.0893 across the six contemporaneous columns; 42,625 calls), and they remain insignificant one quarter ahead (43,049 calls). This extends DWZ's finding that the residual carries no market reaction -- which they document for price and volume -- to the bid-ask spread, a liquidity outcome DWZ did not test, and it sits with BGT's result that the spontaneous response segment does not widen information asymmetry.
intent.reason: This is the load-bearing finding: a clean, consistent null across all twelve specifications. It needs no significance because it is the absence of an association; its weight comes from consistency and from matching DWZ's residual property on a new outcome.

paragraphs.final_prose: The residual carries no such signal. The coefficient on $\mathrm{UncResCEO}$ is small and statistically insignificant in every one of the twelve specifications, whether the spread is measured in the call quarter (the six contemporaneous coefficients range from $-0.0594$ to $-0.1021$; $42{,}625$ calls) or one quarter ahead ($43{,}049$ calls); see Table~\ref{tab:h14c_ceo2_decomp}. \citet{dwz} document this market inertness of the residual for price and volume; here it extends to the bid-ask spread, a liquidity outcome they do not test, and it accords with the \citet{bgt2018} finding that the spontaneous response segment does not widen information asymmetry. The reading is the cautious one: this is an absence of association, not a powered test of equivalence.

intent.statement: The scripted presentation is the segment outsiders price. UncPreCEO loads positively on the contemporaneous spread, significant in four of the six contemporaneous specifications (0.1664, p<0.05, column 1; 0.3496, p<0.01, column 2; 0.2945, p<0.01, column 4; 0.1644, p<0.10, column 6; one-tailed), including all three firm-fixed-effect specifications; it is insignificant in the two industry-fixed-effect specifications with extended controls (columns 3 and 5) and in all six one-quarter-ahead specifications. ClarityCEO is null throughout. This is consistent with BGT's positive presentation-language / information-asymmetry relation (the obfuscation component). It does not contradict the prior finding of no presentation effect on price or volume, because the spread is an information-asymmetry outcome rather than a price or volume reaction.
intent.reason: The positive completes the channel asymmetry but is the weaker, more fragile result; it must be hedged (one-tailed; contemporaneous only; attenuates under industry FE with extended controls) and explicitly reconciled with the prior price/volume null to pre-empt the obvious objection.

paragraphs.final_prose: The scripted presentation behaves differently. The coefficient on $\mathrm{UncPreCEO}$ is positive and significant in four of the six contemporaneous specifications under a one-tailed test ($0.1664$, $p<0.05$, column~1; $0.3496$, $p<0.01$, column~2; $0.2945$, $p<0.01$, column~4; $0.1644$, $p<0.10$, column~6), including all three specifications with firm fixed effects; it is insignificant in the two industry-fixed-effects specifications that add the extended controls (columns~3 and~5) and in all six one-quarter-ahead specifications, while $\mathrm{ClarityCEO}$ is insignificant throughout. This pattern matches the \citet{bgt2018} result that complexity in the scripted presentation is positively associated with information asymmetry. It does not contradict the \citet{dwz} finding of no presentation effect on price or volume, because the bid-ask spread captures information asymmetry rather than a price or volume reaction. The association is, however, contemporaneous and modest, and our linguistic measure is the frequency of uncertainty words rather than the complexity measure of \citet{bgt2018}, so the alignment is one of direction.

intent.statement: Synthesis and the payoff for the main analysis. The two segments of the same call split by audience: the scripted presentation moves the outside information environment (wider contemporaneous spreads), while the improvised residual does not -- a channel asymmetry that sits inside DWZ's own scripted-versus-spontaneous architecture and matches BGT's presentation-versus-response split. The payoff for Section 3: because outsiders do not price the residual, the pre-announcement run-up in the residual cannot be an artifact of outsider reaction; it reads as a private, insider-side signal.
intent.reason: The section earns its place by closing the loop -- naming the channel asymmetry and converting the residual null into an identification shield for the main result, which is the thesis-level reason to run these outcomes at all.

paragraphs.final_prose: Taken together, the two segments of the same call relate to the outside information environment in different ways: the scripted presentation is positively associated with the contemporaneous spread, while the residual shows no detectable association. We do not test the difference between the two components directly, so we read this as a pattern consistent with a channel difference rather than a tested contrast, one that sits within the scripted-versus-spontaneous structure of \citet{dwz} and the presentation-versus-response split of \citet{bgt2018}. Both component readings run with the grain of that prior work: the residual's inertness to the spread extends the market inertness \citet{dwz} document for price and volume to a liquidity outcome they do not test, while the presentation's positive association aligns in direction with \citet{bgt2018}, who find that greater complexity in the scripted presentation is associated with wider information asymmetry.
